correctness.rationale: Averaging the conjugates over coordinate and alphabet permutations preserves all constraints and cannot increase the norm, so the orbit-invariant optimum is global. Tensor characters with k nontrivial factors give normalized eigenvalues by averaging a product of one or two factors chosen from d-k copies of 1 and k copies of -1/u. The resulting spectrum includes every nonconstant mode. For d=2 uniform on all vertices is feasible and unique. For d=3 the quadratic identity 1=3λ1-3λ2+λ3 gives μ≥1/7 with unique equality contacts (1,-1,1)/7, and the corresponding masses are feasible through q=4. For q≥5, λ1≥1-2q/(3u)>0, with equality only at b=1, and the two remaining absolute eigenvalues (2u-1)/(3u²) and 1/u² are smaller. For binary d≥4, λ1≥1-4/d+2a/d and λd=1-2a; intersecting the bounds gives the unique invariant candidate and the centered quadratic λk shows that no intermediate negative eigenvalue exceeds the contact modulus. For nonbinary d≥4, λ1≥1-2q/(du)>0 with equality only at b=1. At b=1 the convex quadratic has maximum at an endpoint and F2(d)=1/u²≤F2(1). Its minimum is bounded below by -1/(d-1) via the square-minus-squares form for d≥5; the listed four values verify the d=4 cases, including the tie when q=3. Radius-one endpoint balancing gives exactly half the optimal absolute spectral gap, with averaging valid there as well. Phase statements are understood in the indicated invariant family, not as a claim that every unrestricted optimizer is uniform.
residual_risks: Supplied finite-grid, LP and full-matrix routines were inspected, not run. They are corroboration, not the all-parameter proof. No unrestricted uniqueness claim except d=2.

evidence: Theorem 2.1 and its corollaries of arXiv:0709.0955 supply the symmetry reduction. The Hamming calculation of §3.3.3 assigns weight to distance-one edges only. The hypercube cutoff paper is a plausible antecedent for binary cases, but its full text was not reached.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The generic averaging and SDP formulations reduce the feasible set but supply no solution to the nonbinary two-orbit quadratic minimax problem. The earlier radius-one optimum is a baseline, not an upper or lower certificate of equality for the radius-two optimum.

evidence: On the halved binary cube, the simple-walk eigenvalues are 1-4k(d-k+1)/(d(d+1)); the edge-transitive formula compares the two spectral extremes and recovers the binary optimizer, including the d=3 need for holding. The nonbinary case instead needs the feasibility cutoff of the three-contact certificate and control of a different quadratic on every mode.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Known symmetry and spectral data imply a one-variable closed optimization for the binary slice. For nonbinary q the generic reduction still leaves a constrained minimax over two masses; the q=4 and q=5 boundaries and complete spectral upper certificate are not the radius-one or edge-transitive theorem specialized.

Appending the parity bit identifies the binary radius-two graph with the even half of the (d+1)-cube, adjacent at distance two. Coordinate permutations and even translations are edge-transitive.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The binary problem is an instance of the known edge-transitive theorem with the halved-cube spectrum; do not claim the binary allocation in isolation as a new optimization principle. In the nonbinary problem there are two distance weights, with actual mixed or boundary optima depending on dimension and alphabet; neither the binary reduction nor the ordinary Hamming result covers that family. Exact later overlap does not establish earlier publication or independent provenance.

value.rationale: Allowing the next Hamming radius is a natural change to a canonical mixing graph. The exact minimax result identifies which transitions and holding are beneficial and quantifies the SLEM-gap gain. In three dimensions the interpolation contacts and feasibility cutoff explain why distance-one moves and then holding disappear at different alphabet sizes. That boundary information is not a trivial restatement of symmetry or of the existing distance-one optimum.
residual_risks: No claim of equal per-step computational cost or comparable total-variation distance at each time, or of optimality for nonsymmetric kernels.
